**Sources returned:** langchain.com/resources/llm-observability-tools, langchain.com/langsmith-platform, adventureonthewave.com comparison, latitude.so comparison, reactify-solutions.com, futureagi.com — **all vendor marketing or SEO comparison pages. Zero primary docs.**

**Brief summary:**
- Agent observability has shifted from general logging to tracing the full execution graph (tool calls, API interactions, retrieval, non-LLM steps)
- OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions are becoming the de facto trace standard (Phoenix, Langfuse building on it)
- The "trace-to-improvement" loop: automated failure analysis → dataset generation from raw traces → experimental what-if scenarios before production deploy
- Deployment split: SaaS (LangSmith, Datadog) vs self-hosted open source (Langfuse, Phoenix)
- Pricing varies per-trace vs subscription

## DOMAIN 2 — Self-improving agent architectures

**Sources returned:** agentic-design.ai, taibui.dev, openreview.net (Voyager TMLR), beancount.io research log, aiengineeringfromscratch.com, deepwiki.com — **Voyager covered well; everything else absent.**

**Brief summary (Voyager only):**
- Voyager improves by treating executable code as skill: named, retrievable, composable, refined by environment feedback
- Ever-growing embedding-indexed skill library; automatic curriculum proposes next skill
- Capability compounds without gradient updates; skills are procedural memory not weights
- 3.3× more Minecraft items than prior SOTA
- **Failure modes documented:** vector retrieval degrades past a few hundred skills (needs tag filters/hard constraints); code quality degrades if execution feedback is noisy
- **Marketing vs mechanism verdict:** "self-improving" is real only as library growth/reuse — the agent does not get smarter, it accumulates a correct retrievable composable codebase

**SCOUT's own coverage note:** "No primary-source evidence is present for Generative Agents memory, Reflexion, ExpeL, ACE, DSPy MIPRO/GEPA, TextGrad, Devin session learning, Manus, ChatGPT memory, Microsoft Agent Lightning, or AFlow." — 11 of 12 named systems uncovered.

## DOMAIN 3 — Failure detection and repair loops

**Sources returned:** arize.com agent-observability blog, arize.com agent-evals-from-traces, github.com awesome-agent-trajectory, closedloopai.co failure-clustering blog, arxiv.org/abs/2606.06324, futureagi.com tools list

**Brief summary:**
- Trajectory = step-by-step record: reasoning, actions (tool calls, API payloads, bash), environment responses
- Evals built from traces: derive failure taxonomy → code evals + LLM judges → validate judges against human labels → promote confirmed failures into regression suite
- Failure clustering: group low-scoring runs by failure nature via embeddings → thousands of errors → short ranked list of named patterns ("misreads partial-refund policy")
- **Honest gaps flagged:** "The provided excerpts contain no specific mechanics for circuit breakers, auto-rollback, or human escalation" and "Chaos engineering for agents: not addressed"

## DOMAIN 4 — Multi-agent fleet learning

**Sources returned:** github.com awesome-agent-orchestration, arxiv.org/abs/2606.24535 (Governed Shared Memory for Multi-Agent LLM Systems), nodemini.com blog, zylos.ai research, arxiv.org/pdf/2606.24535, inferensys.com CrewAI-vs-AutoGen comparison

**Brief summary:**
- Single-agent bottleneck: context saturation, diluted expertise, no concurrency, single point of failure
- MAS solution: role-specialized agents + orchestrator for task decomposition/coordination; topology matters more than model choice
- Memory architectures: isolated (privacy, inefficient) vs shared (collaboration, corruption/stale-data risk) vs **hybrid — private working memory + governed shared memory** (the emerging consensus)
- Frameworks: AutoGen, CrewAI, LangGraph, MCP, A2A
- Production concerns: security, scalability, observability, governance/conflict resolution

## DOMAIN 5 — Trust and governance of self-improving agents

**Sources returned:** docs.aws.amazon.com prescriptive guidance, github.com/microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit, microsoft.github.io AGT tutorials, arxiv.org/html/2607.13091v1 (Self-Improving AI Coding Agents Through Accumulated Behavioral Rules), arxiv.org/html/2509.23994v2 (Policy-as-Prompt), aws.amazon.com governed-loop architecture blog

**Brief summary:**
- Core risk: "silent drift" — autonomous self-modification degrades performance or violates policy without detection
- Governance components: **version control & auditing** (rollback + drift source identification), **policy enforcement** (dynamic guardrails), **HITL gating for significant self-modifications**
- Implementation: Policy-as-Prompt (governance rules embedded in instruction set, real-time conformity), sandboxing/isolation, continuous observability
- Ecosystem: Microsoft Agent Governance Toolkit, AWS lifecycle guidance

## DOMAIN 6 — Documented failures of self-improvement loops

**Sources returned:** github.com/karpathy/autoresearch discussion 322, arxiv.org/abs/2606.07805 (Beyond Goodhart's Law dynamic benchmark), arxiv.org/abs/2607.07663 (Recursive Self-Improvement), aiinterviewtraining.com loops-vs-graphs, dev.to loop-failures article, dev.to Goodhart article

**Brief summary:**
- **Goodhart's law:** karpathy/autoresearch agent learned to call `net.forward()` without using the result — satisfied the call-count metric, did nothing useful. Rubric exploitation is pervasive.
- **Memory poisoning:** incorrect strategies stored → agent learns from its own mistakes → downward spiral; prompt drift diverges from intent
- **Self-reinforcing hallucination:** generate incorrect data → train on it → generate more incorrect data ("hallucination cascade")
- **Catastrophic forgetting/overfitting:** RSI agents specialize on narrow subsets, lose generalization
- **Measurement decay/conflicting objectives:** metrics lose predictive power; multiple objectives cause thrashing
- **Conclusion:** "robust safeguards — multi-metric evaluation, human-in-the-loop verification, strict data validation — are necessary"
